title: bus.deploy.stale v1
description: Emitted by the deploy-staleness monitor adapter (adapters/deploy-staleness/) when a long-running process (systemd user unit or AppImage-style unmanaged process) is found running code older than the code currently on disk -- e.g. a binary replaced by a fix while the old build keeps serving traffic, or a fuse-mounted AppImage that pins its old contents after the underlying file is overwritten. Watches the deploys: makes 'merged + tests green + still running the stale build' visible instead of discoverable only by a manual sweep.

target.description: systemd unit name (e.g. kb-watch.service) or process matcher name (e.g. appimage:orca) that this event describes

kind.description: 'unit' for a systemd --user managed service, 'process' for an unmanaged long-running process matched by roster.json appimage_matchers

pid.description: PID of the running process this verdict was computed against, when known

verdict.description: This event is only ever published on a transition; 'stale' means the running process predates its code, 'fresh' means a previously-stale target recovered (restarted onto current code)

reason.description: Which freshness signal drove the verdict: script/binary mtime, a later git commit touching the source file, /proc/<pid>/exe resolving to a deleted (replaced) binary, an AppImage-style file newer than the process that mounted it, or a fresh-after-stale recovery

running_since.description: RFC3339 UTC timestamp the running process/unit started

code_newest_at.description: RFC3339 UTC timestamp of the newest freshness signal found for the code backing this target (max of file mtime and, for git-tracked sources, last commit touching the file)

remedy_hint.description: Human-actionable next step, e.g. 'systemctl --user restart kb-watch.service' or 'relaunch orca (kill pid 1500947)'
